title: A great month for the team
body: Your boss has told the floor above about the good work your boss has been doing on your project. It is your work, and it has been described with great accuracy. Your name is in the copy line.

from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
title: Your figures have been presented
body: The Senior Analyst has shown your figures to the floor above, with one small improvement: a different name is now in the corner where yours was. An email thanks the team for its support.

title: FW: Monthly Status Report OVERDUE
body: Your boss has forwarded you a chaser about the report you did not file. The whole message reads: Thoughts?

title: Thanks for your input
body: Your Monthly Status Report has gone upstairs under your boss's name, as an executive summary of your Monthly Status Report. The summary is your report.

title: You hear your phrase on the way up
body: Your boss is explaining strategic patience to someone from the fifth floor, and is doing so as its author. You are holding the door.

title: Your desk has been moved
body: As part of the Workplace Refresh, your desk is now next to the printer, and has no window. Somebody has been given the one with the window, and nobody will say who decided.

title: Your project is apparently in trouble
body: Someone from another team asks kindly how you are coping. You did not know that you were coping with anything. It seems to be widely known that your project is in trouble.

falseStory.text: A story that your project was in trouble.

from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
title: RE: The figures you needed by Tuesday
body: The Project Co-ordinator has sent you the figures you needed. It is Wednesday. The Project Co-ordinator's message adds that they are sorry for the delay, and that the whole team has been copied in, along with your deadline.

from: From: The Office Co-ordinator, Marjorie Tull
title: Invitation updated
body: A meeting you were preparing for has moved to yesterday. The minutes are attached. You were present, and you agreed to several things.

from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
title: Those laptops
body: The Senior Analyst has told several people that you promised the team new laptops. You did not. You have now been asked when they will arrive, by someone who does not believe you.

from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
title: A question from the floor
body: You gave a short update to people from upstairs. The Senior Analyst asked, very pleasantly, one question about a number on your third slide. Nobody had looked at that number until then. They are all looking at it now.

title: The offsite: a small ask
body: The board has arranged an offsite. You are to give a two-hour presentation on your project, and you have until tomorrow. A later message says that it has been moved to the afternoon slot, and cut to four minutes, and that it is no longer needed.

title: A brief, informal conversation
body: Someone has raised a concern about your schedule, in confidence. Human Resources would like you to know that they cannot say who, or about what, and that this will not affect anything. A date has been put in your calendar.

title: A small favour
body: Your boss's boss has put you on a working group about working groups, on the basis of a conversation you do not remember. It meets on Fridays, and it has no end date.

from: From: The Project Co-ordinator, Callum Reed
title: About that favour
body: The Project Co-ordinator is still on the supplier's team, and would like you to know that they have not forgotten. They would like you to cover the supplier's Friday call, which is three hours long and in a time zone. Since you owe them, you do.

from: From: The Senior Analyst, Priya Venn
title: About that favour
body: The Senior Analyst needs someone to check four hundred rows of figures by hand, because the system is not trusted. They remind you, pleasantly, about the footer. You spend an evening on rows.

title: Somebody else's long evenings
body: {competitor} is telling someone from the floor above about this month's figures, and the long evenings that went into them. They were your figures, and your evenings.

title: Action: you
body: The draft minutes of a meeting you were not invited to record that the delay to your project began with you. {competitor} raised it, with regret, and has kindly offered to help you catch up.

from: Your update to the floor above
title: Just one more question
body: You gave a short update to people from upstairs. At the very end {competitor} asked, warmly, what the plan was if the dates slipped. You had no plan for that, and now everyone knows that you had no plan for that.

title: Figures, as per your request
body: Since the seat went the way it did, the Senior Analyst sends you exactly what you ask for, to the letter, and nothing that you needed. It arrives on time. It is all correct, and none of it is any use.

title: An update on your dependencies
body: The Project Co-ordinator has noticed, since the seat was decided, that your work depends on several things. Each is now on a tracker, red, with your name beside it.

title: A quiet word upstairs
body: Since the seat was filled, the Junior Associate has been having coffee with people from Floor 3. Your name comes up, you hear, as a cautionary example of something.

title: RE: RE: RE: Please remove me from this list
body: Someone in another building has replied to everyone in the company asking to be taken off the list. Four hundred people have replied to everyone asking the same. You spend the morning not replying, which takes concentration.

title: Your access card has been reset
body: Your access card stopped working overnight, as part of a security improvement. You spend the morning in reception, where you are signed in as a visitor to your own desk, and escorted to it.

title: An update on organisational design
body: An e-mail explains that the organisation is being redesigned around the customer. There is a diagram with the customer in the middle. Your team is in a box at the edge marked Enablers, which is nearer the customer than it sounds.

title: Thanks to everyone who made it happen
body: {competitor} has sent round an e-mail thanking everyone who made the Grand Plan happen, at some length, and signing it as its lead. Your name is in the list of everyone.

title: Who really did the Grand Plan
body: You hear, in the lift, that you had very little to do with the Grand Plan. You hear it from someone who heard it from {competitor}, who was only saying.

title: A long lunch
body: {competitor}'s calendar has a two-hour lunch in it, marked Private, at the place upstairs goes to. It is the week the seat is decided.

title: Weekly fire alarm test
body: The weekly fire alarm test goes off during your one important call of the month. It is followed by an announcement that it was only a test, and then by the alarm again, to be sure.

title: A meeting about meetings
body: You are invited to a meeting about having fewer meetings. It is recurring. The first one overruns, and a follow-up is booked to discuss why.
